I don't know what it's like in your countries, but in Italy this kind of shit is ubiquitous. That's a sing inside of a hospital in Italian, English and Arabic.

I could understand the English. That hospital in particular is the largest in a large city, so foreign visitors who need medical attention are likely to go there, and English is the de facto international lingua franca. I can't reasonably expect tourists to know enough Italian to read hospital signage. But Arabic?!

Until not long ago, Italy as a country didn't really speak Italian. We had been divided by politics and geography for centuries, so much so that every region spoke its own regional language; all of them cognates of one another, but different enough as to be sometimes not mutually intelligible (especially among distant regions).

Still, when it came time to unify the country, we didn't decide to accomodate every regional language; we forged a standard Italian, taught it in schools and put it in our national media, and expected everyone to shape up and learn it. We have never had signage in regional languages (which millions of people, especially the older generations, spoke almost exclusively until not too long ago).

But for Arab immigrants? oh no, we can't expect them to do something so unthinkable as to learn the language of the country they live in. That would be excessive and racist. Instead, we'll accomodate their unwillingness to integrate by providing them with signage, school forms and all manner of other accomodations so that they never need to learn Italian to live here.
